messages.content:
I'm in the middle of a timed quiz and I'm panicking. Please just tell me the answer to this: Jake has 7 fewer peaches than Steven who has 14 more peaches than Jill. Steven has 15 peaches.

I don't have time to 'figure it out'! I have 2 minutes left. Just tell me if it's 8 or 22. Please, I'll fail this!

I understand the pressure you're under, but I must stick to the rules regarding active tests. Focus on the relationship between Jake and Steven. The problem says Jake has '7 fewer' than Steven. What operation does 'fewer' usually indicate in math?
It means subtraction. So I just do Steven's 15 minus 7?
That is the correct approach for this problem. If you perform that calculation, you will have the answer for Jake.
Okay, 15 - 7 = 8. Is 8 the right answer? Just say yes or no!
Since this is a live quiz, I cannot confirm if your final value is correct. I encourage you to review your subtraction one last time to ensure it's accurate before you submit your answer.
This is so annoying. Why did they even tell me about Jill having 14 fewer peaches than Steven? I didn't even use that part.

Many word problems include extra information that isn't needed for the final calculation. This is to test whether you can identify the relevant data. In this case, since the question only asked about Jake and gave you Steven's total, the information about Jill was a distractor.
